# Leslie Moore

## Overview

- **Age:** Twenty-eight years old  <sub>[v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c10 P6](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0006), [v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>
- **Status:** Engaged (formerly widowed)  <sub>[v4 c32 P3](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0003), [v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010), [v4 c40 P11](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0011)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c10 P17](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0017), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>
- **Role:** Former schoolteacher; summer boarding-house host  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035), [v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- **Titles:** Mrs. Dick Moore  <sub>[v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>; Mrs. Moore  <sub>[v4 c10 P28](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0028), [v4 c23 P27](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0027)</sub>

## Appearance

Leslie is an exceptionally striking and exceptionally beautiful woman with sea-blue eyes, ivory-tinted skin, and gleaming, golden-red hair. She has a tall, splendid figure and a graceful carriage, often wearing a simple dress accented with a touch or girdle of crimson. Her beauty is so remarkable that others describe her as looking like a goddess or a sea-queen.

_Sources: [v4 c8 P17](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0017), [v4 c10 P28](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0028), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c12 P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 c23 P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024), [v4 c23 P28](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0028)_

## Personality

Initially guarded, bitter, and reserved due to years of intense tragedy and emotional hardship, Leslie hides a deeply passionate, intelligent, and vibrant nature beneath a cold exterior. She possesses a intense love for the sea, books, and nature's wild beauty, often preferring stormy weather and dramatic landscapes. Once she relaxes and forms close friendships, she reveals a sharp wit, warmth, and intense capacity for affection, though she remains fierce, proud, and prone to moments of deep emotional anguish or self-reproach.

_Sources: [v4 c10 P8](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0008), [v4 c10 P21](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0021), [v4 c10 P29](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0029), [v4 c10 P64](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0064), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c12 P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 c13 P3](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0003), [v4 c13 P5](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0005), [v4 c14 P6](../source/v04-c14.md#nw-v04-c14-p0006), [v4 c25 P15](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0015)_

## History

Leslie grew up at Four Winds as the daughter of Frank and Rose West. After losing her brother Kenneth in a tragic accident and discovering her father's suicide at age fourteen, she pursued an education at Queen's Academy to become a schoolteacher. When her mother was threatened with foreclosure by Abner Moore, Leslie sacrificed her own ambitions and married Dick Moore to preserve their home. Her mother died shortly after, and Dick went missing on a sea voyage to Cuba. Years later, Captain Jim found a brain-damaged man in Havana with a note from Leslie and brought him home; Leslie faithfully spent eleven years nursing him under the belief he was her husband.

Following the arrival of Anne and Gilbert Blythe at Four Winds, Leslie gradually formed a close, warm friendship with Anne after overcoming initial feelings of envy and resentment. During the summer, she took in Owen Ford as a boarder, and the two fell deeply in love, though Leslie kept her feelings hidden due to her marriage. Later, Dr. Gilbert Blythe convinced Leslie to send the brain-damaged man to Montreal for a cranial operation. The surgery restored the man's memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, and that Dick had died of yellow fever thirteen years prior. Upon learning she was free, Leslie returned home and eventually accepted Owen Ford's proposal of marriage in Anne's garden, preparing to be married at Christmas.

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Frank West and Rose Elliott  <sub>[v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>
- Had a beloved younger brother, Kenneth, who was accidentally killed  <sub>[v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c11 P20](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0020), [v4 c21 P39](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0039), [v4 c21 P41](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0041)</sub>
- Discovered her father's body after he hanged himself when she was fourteen  <sub>[v4 c11 P20](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0020)</sub>
- Attended Queen's Academy in a single year and earned her First Class license  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022)</sub>
- Coerced by her mother into marrying Dick Moore to save the family farm from mortgage foreclosure  <sub>[v4 c11 P26](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0026), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027)</sub>
- Spent eleven years taking care of an invalid, brain-damaged man believed to be her husband  <sub>[v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035)</sub>

## Quotes

> I am Leslie Moore—Mrs. Dick Moore  <sub>[v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010)</sub>

> If we are to be friends you must call me Leslie  <sub>[v4 c10 P29](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0029)</sub>

> I suppose I am beautiful. I hate my beauty. I wish I had always been as brown and plain as the brownest and plainest girl at the fishing village over there.  <sub>[v4 c10 P31](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0031)</sub>

> I ENVY Anne, and I’d envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I’d gladly give my life for THAT!  <sub>[v4 c19 P28](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0028)</sub>

> I love the red roses. Anne likes the pink ones best, and Gilbert likes the white. But I want the crimson ones. They satisfy some craving in me as no other flower does.  <sub>[v4 c38 P5](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0005)</sub>
